frases.texto: This survey reviews recent advances from 2021 to 2025 in automatic fetal head and brain segmentation and biometric estimation.
Accurate fetal biometric parameters, such as head circumference, biparietal diameter, and occipitofrontal diameter of the head are important for prenatal diagnosis and growth tracking.
convolutional neural networks, encoder decoder architectures, and hybrid attention mechanisms have greatly increased segmentation accuracy and speed.

This study also summarizes dataset features, evaluation metrics, and benchmark results, highlighting the lack of a standard ultrasound dataset as a key limitation.

Here, we conducted a systematic review of articles describing predictive models integrated into EHR systems and implemented in clinical practice.

The most common clinical domains of implemented predictive models were related to thrombotic disorders/anticoagulation (25%) and sepsis (16%).
We obtained an initial 3393 articles for screening, from which a final set of 44 articles was included for data extraction and analysis.

Micro-lip-reading is an emerging research area that aims to recognize speech by observing subtle and fast lip movements.
[título] A Review on Event-Augmented, Audio-Visual Distillation for MicroLip-Reading with Tiny Transformers

tiny transformer architectures allow for efficient modeling of temporal and spatial patterns across audio, RGB, and event modalities, while knowledge distillation techniques help transfer information from large models to smaller, edge-friendly models
This review presents an overview of event-based and audiovisual fusion approaches, benchmark datasets, evaluation metrics, and practical deployment strategies.

This research investigates recent developments in Deep Learning (DL) and Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for skin cancer diagnosis striking a balance between model accuracy and clinical interpretability.
The large number of skin cancer cases need early detection with accuracy to reduce mortality rate.
Well known DL models like ResNet50, DenseNet121, InceptionV3, EfficientNetB0, and hybrid architectures including HRNet-XGB are studied and compared.
this research suggests future paths including multimodal data integration, clinician-in-the-loop evaluation, and mobile-compatible deployments.

the objective of the present review is to investigate how AR visualization can integrate data from Internet of Things devices, unmanned aerial vehicles, farming machinery, robotics, edge computing platforms and artificial intelligence (AI) to enable their coordinated, field-level deployment in precision agriculture.
The integration of augmented reality (AR) into embedded agricultural systems is reshaping precision farming by enabling real-time visualizations and interactions with complex environmental data.

The article offers three primary contributions: a structured synthesis of AR applications across embedded systems, a conceptual architecture for AR-centered smart farming and an integrated analysis of research gaps and future directions.

Key research gaps include the lack of studies addressing model interpretability and system interoperability, insufficient exploration of real-time edge AI processing and gesture-based AR controls, and the absence of globally representative data sets for AI image analysis.
This review systematically bridges the gap between algorithmic innovation and hardware-aware deployment by presenting a critical analysis spanning three interconnected dimensions

Continuous integration and deployment (CI/CD) pipelines, which are infamous for their slowness, frequent failures, and protracted build times, are a crucial part of the modern software development process.

This systematic literature review synthesizes peer-reviewed studies on lightweight YOLO models published from 2016 to 2025.
Object detection is a core task in computer vision, and the You Only Look Once (YOLO) family remains a preferred choice for real-time applications.
lightweight YOLO variants

We classify primary lightweighting strategies—pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, and lightweight network architectures—and evaluate their trade-offs in accuracy, latency, model size, and energy use.
We also examine application domains, dataset effects, common evaluation metrics, and deployment platforms (e.g., Jetson, Raspberry Pi, microcontrollers, Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs))
This paper reviews a novel LLM-powered pipeline for generating resumes that are dynamically tailored to job descriptions and optimised for Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS).
most resumes are filtered before reaching a recruiter, primarily because of the rigid keyword-matching and formatting rules enforced by ATS algorithms.
LLM-powered
By combining structured parsing, semantic alignment, and iterative scoring, our system overcomes these limitations and generates highly customised, ATS-friendly resumes

We demonstrate, through token-based and latent-space evaluations, that our optimised resumes nearly double their effectiveness compared to unmodified versions, improving alignment scores on average by 85%.
we propose FineST, a scheduling framework for serving DNNs with fine-grained spatio-temporal sharing of GPU inference servers.
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) are commonly deployed as online inference services.
Deep Neural Networks (DNNs)

To maximize GPU utilization, FineST allocates intra-GPU computing resources from both spatial and temporal dimensions across DNNs in a cost-effective way, while predicting interference overheads under diverse consolidated executions for controlling SLO violation rates.
Compared to a state-of-the-art work, FineST improves the peak throughput of serving heterogeneous DNNsby up to 64.7% under SLO constraints.

This article comprehensively reviews embedded systems technology applied to electrical machines.
electrical machines have been garnering increased attention due to their numerous advantages, leading to the evolution of various high-performance control techniques.
This work contributes to the state of the art in embedded systems for power electronic converters and control systems for electrical drives.

In this paper, we present a comprehensive review of ultrasound clutter suppression techniques and exploit the feasibility of low-rank and sparse decomposition schemes in ultrasound clutter suppression.
Vessel diseases are often accompanied by abnormalities related to vascular shape and size.
A potential solution to these issues is using decomposition into low-rank and sparse matrices (DLSM) framework.
We conduct this review study by adapting 106 DLSM algorithms and validating them against simulation, phantom, and in vivo rat datasets.
This paper presents a concise review and unified discussion of Gaussian-based sparseview reconstruction methods from the perspective of energyefficient and sustainable AI.
Neural 3D scene representation methods have enabled significant advances in photorealistic reconstruction and novel view synthesis, but often at the cost of high computational and energy demands.
3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently emerged as an efficient alternative that replaces implicit neural fields with explicit Gaussian primitives and rasterization-style rendering

recent extensions such as Few-Shot Gaussian Splatting (FSGS) and Co-Regularized Gaussian Splatting (CoR-GS) introduce principled strategies for initialization, densification, pruning, and supervision that improve stability without reintroducing computationally expensive neural rendering.
